title: The wait a software company's benefits portal should quote for the work-permit renewals its global mobility team files from January to March 2027
subdomain: regression, classification and model diagnostics (employer immigration operations: a forward 80th percentile of a censored wait under the stage model the record supports, each renewal cut at its own card's expiry by the team's expedite request)
prompt_shape: one quoted wait to the nearest half month with its components; permits expiring in each of three months by category; lockbox rejections and refilings within 30 days in each of four quarters; a labelled bar chart of the permits expiring

distractors.why_relevant: the team's record of the processing time USCIS posts for Form I-765, which people quote back
distractors.why_unused: USCIS's figure covers every filer nationally and the cases it completed in past months, not the renewals Global Mobility files in the coming quarter (standard GM-07, 4.1); no figure reads it
distractors.ruled_out_by: the file's own form lines and offices, and standard GM-07 4.1 to 4.2

distractors.why_relevant: H-4 spouses' work permits run to the H-4 end date the principal's H-1B sets
distractors.why_unused: it lists H-1B extensions to file in 2027, not work permits; no figure reads it

sources.origin: constructed for this task by task172/generator/build.py (seeded, deterministic) around a fictional software company in Bellevue, Washington (Sallowmere Software), its fictional outside counsel (Marrowby Teale LLP) and its employees, identified by number only. No real organisation's records or person is depicted. USCIS notices, receipt numbers, card numbers and processing times are constructed in their real formats and are not USCIS data.
